newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asia Securities takes stake in vessels.
newsitem.headline: Asia Securities takes stake in vessels.

text.p: Asia Securities International Ltd said it would buy 91 percent stakes in five bulk carriers from third-party China National Foreign Trade Transportation Corp of Beijing (Sinotrans) for HK$495.15 million.

Asia Securities and Bengal Star Investment Corp, a unit of Sinotrans, would jointly buy the vessels from Sinotrans for a total HK$544.12 million, with Asia Securities taking 91 percent and Bengal nine percent, the company said in a statement.

Asia Securities said it had paid HK$49.52 million, or 10 percent of its share of the purchase, on signing of the agreement, and the company would use its own internal resources to fund its remaining share of the purchase.

Asia Securities said Sinotrans had also undertaken to the company a guaranteed rate of return of 4.5 percent for the first 12 months period following completion of the deal, and 8.5 percent for the second 12 months period.
"The directors believe that the shipping industry as a whole is on a gradual recovery," Asia Securities said.
"The directors therefore consider that the shipping business possesses potential for high growth and will generate recurring income and long-term capital gains in future," it said.
